trial_title: Methadone, Morphine, or Oxycodone in Treating Pain in Patients With Cancer
brief_summary:
RATIONALE: Methadone, morphine, or oxycodone may help relieve pain caused by cancer. It is not yet known whether methadone is more effective than morphine or oxycodone in treating pain in patients with cancer.

PURPOSE: This randomized clinical trial is studying methadone to see how well it works compared with morphine or oxycodone in treating pain in patients with cancer.

eligibility_table.criterion: Receiving ongoing care in the outpatient medical oncology setting
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is receiving ongoing care for their conditions, including treatment for anaplastic astrocytoma.

eligibility_table.criterion: Self-reported pain (of any cause) for which long-acting strong opioids (morphine or oxycodone) have been prescribed or administered
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has chronic pain and is on high-dose steroids, which suggests they may be receiving strong opioids.

eligibility_table.criterion: Oral morphine-equivalent daily dose (MEDD) of existing opioid regimen (long-acting or immediate-release) 40-300 mg/day
eligibility_table.justification: The specific oral morphine-equivalent daily dose (MEDD) is not provided in the profile.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: What is the patient's current oral morphine-equivalent daily dose (MEDD) of their existing opioid regimen?

eligibility_table.criterion: Worst pain score on a scale of 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst pain) of ≥ 5 for ≥ 1 week duration based on verbal self-report AND/OR ≥ 1 persistently bothersome symptom attributed to an opioid side effect
eligibility_table.justification: The worst pain score is not explicitly mentioned in the profile.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient reported a worst pain score of ≥5 on a scale of 0 to 10 for at least one week?

eligibility_table.criterion: None of the following conditions that could predispose the patient to prolonged QT interval-associated tachycardia:
eligibility_table.justification: There is no indication of conditions that predispose the patient to prolonged QT interval-associated tachycardia.

eligibility_table.criterion: Serum potassium < 3.0 mg/dL
eligibility_table.justification: Serum potassium levels are not provided in the profile.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient's serum potassium level currently < 3.0 mg/dL?

eligibility_table.criterion: Cocaine abuse within the past 3 months
eligibility_table.justification: There is no mention of cocaine abuse in the patient's history.

eligibility_table.criterion: Family history of sudden death
eligibility_table.justification: There is no indication of a family history of sudden death in the profile.

eligibility_table.criterion: Advanced heart failure (ejection fraction < 40% and/or New York Heart Association (NYHA) class III or IV heart disease)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's ejection fraction or NYHA class is not provided, so advanced heart failure status is unknown.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have an ejection fraction of less than 40% or a New York Heart Association (NYHA) classification of III or IV?

eligibility_table.criterion: No known or suspected cognitive impairment that could interfere with adherence to the medication plan or self-report of symptoms and side effects
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information regarding cognitive impairment in the patient's profile.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a documented cognitive assessment score of ≥24 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE)?

eligibility_table.criterion: Not pregnant or nursing
eligibility_table.justification: Category not evaluable deterministically
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient currently pregnant or nursing?

eligibility_table.criterion: Fertile patients must use effective contraception
eligibility_table.justification: Patient's fertility status and contraception use are not provided.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient currently using an effective form of contraception, such as a hormonal method, barrier method, or intrauterine device, as defined by clinical guidelines?

eligibility_table.criterion: More than 4 weeks since prior radiotherapy or surgery for local control of cancer or pain palliation
eligibility_table.justification: Category not evaluable deterministically
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient undergone any radiotherapy or surgery for local control of cancer or pain palliation within the last 4 weeks?

eligibility_table.criterion: More than 60 days since prior use of the same long-acting opioid (i.e., the new long-acting opioid) that patient is switching to on the study
eligibility_table.justification: Category not evaluable deterministically
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient used any long-acting opioid within the last 60 days?

eligibility_table.criterion: More than 12 weeks since prior methadone therapy
eligibility_table.justification: Category not evaluable deterministically
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient completed methadone therapy more than 12 weeks ago?

eligibility_table.criterion: More than 3 days since prior and no concurrent transdermal fentanyl, oxymorphone, or buprenorphine
eligibility_table.justification: Category not evaluable deterministically
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient received any transdermal fentanyl, oxymorphone, or buprenorphine in the past 3 days?

eligibility_table.criterion: Concurrent systemic anticancer therapy or bisphosphonates allowed provided therapy was initiated ≥ 4 weeks ago
eligibility_table.justification: Patient's systemic therapy (Avastin and CPT-11) was initiated more than 4 weeks ago.

eligibility_table.criterion: Concurrent tricyclic antidepressants, Nonsteroidal Antiinflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs), anticonvulsants, or other adjuvant analgesics or psychostimulants allowed provided therapy was initiated ≥ 2 weeks ago
eligibility_table.justification: Patient is on high-dose steroids and other medications, but no specific start date is provided; however, they are likely to have been on them for more than 2 weeks.

eligibility_table.criterion: Dose expected to remain stable until after the first week of opioid rotation on study
eligibility_table.justification: No information on whether the dose of opioids is stable or if opioid rotation is planned.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient's opioid dose remained stable for at least 7 days prior to the rotation to methadone, morphine, or oxycodone?

eligibility_table.criterion: No concurrent methadone maintenance therapy for opioid addiction
eligibility_table.justification: No mention of methadone maintenance therapy for opioid addiction.

eligibility_table.criterion: No concurrent intrathecal infusion of analgesics
eligibility_table.justification: No mention of concurrent intrathecal infusion of analgesics.

eligibility_table.criterion: No concurrent antiarrhythmic medications (e.g., amiodarone or quinidine)
eligibility_table.justification: No mention of concurrent antiarrhythmic medications.
